SURFACE: 2-col file, no header. Numbers like "47183,554644" — comma as decimal mark (German/EU locale), tab between cols. Col1 descending 47183→1648 (looks like wavenumber axis). Col2 noisy ~5800-19800 (intensity/counts).

CONTENT: Comma really is decimal separator here, not thousands-grouping — 6-digit fraction after comma rules out grouping. Real check against graphene physics: G peak ~1580 cm⁻¹, 2D peak ~2700 cm⁻¹. Sample tail (last 20 rows) sits at x≈1648-1653, near-but-above G peak; head sits at x≈47183, way past any normal Raman shift window (usually <4000 cm⁻¹). Full 3565-row range not shown, so can't confirm both peaks fall inside data — worth checking before fit.

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

MISREADINGS:
1. Naive CSV parser splits on comma (assume US/CSV convention) → mangles each number into two fields or reads as giant int (47183554646). Evidence: comma sits mid-number consistently, tab is real field sep.
2. Peak-fit/interpolation code assumes ascending x → data descending row1→row3565. Evidence: shown head (47183) > tail (1648), monotonic drop.
3. Treating col1 as literal Raman shift cm⁻¹ without sanity-check → max value 47183 is ~15-30x typical graphene Raman range (G/2D live under 3000 cm⁻¹). Risk: axis may need trim/calibration, or large stretch of "spectrum" (down to ~4000) is empty/irrelevant to G,2D fit. Evidence: known G≈1580, 2D≈2700 cm⁻¹ vs data ceiling 47183.
4. Column swap risk — assuming col2 is x-axis. Evidence: col1 is smooth monotonic (axis-like), col2 is noisy (signal-like) — confirms col1=x, col2=intensity.
